notes:
Account summary: Tessera is a large omnichannel contact center operator (BPO + in-house teams). Heavy seasonal spikes (holiday retail clients) and unpredictable incident bursts when upstream CRM/API outages occur. Primary want: make agent-assist and live tool-calling reliable under 3x-10x traffic bursts without human reroute. They have existing Genesys front-end and want inference to sit behind a service layer.

Recent timeline / activity:
- 2025-09-10: Initial inbound via marketing whitepaper. AE Sofia assigned.
- 2025-09-22: Discovery call (FF-2025-09-22-1012) w/ Head of Automation (Maya Chen) + SRE. Key ask: keep mean agent assist latency <50ms 99th under spikes; guarantee fallback to cached responses.
- 2025-10-07: Tech deep-dive (FF-2025-10-07-0930). SE Ravi demoed routing rules, canary/fallback, and pre-warm pools. Collecting sample traffic (anonymized) for capacity model.
- 2025-10-15: Contract & security kickoff. Legal requested SOC2 + data residency addendum.
- 2025-10-28: POC kickoff meeting (FF-2025-10-28-1543). Agreed 2-week stress POC: simulate 5x and 10x bursts, include incident burst scenario (CRM outage causing retry storms).
- 2025-10-29 - 2025-11-01: Run #1 POC - baseline with hosted setup + prewarm pools. Observed token cost higher than expected; latency 95th ~62ms under 5x with prewarm; 95th >120ms under 10x. SE notes: need dedicated reserved capacity or autoscale faster with cold-start mitigation.
- 2025-11-03: Follow-up with SRE - presented recommended config (dedicated pools + prefix KV caching + fallback smaller model for hot paths).

Technical requirements / acceptance criteria:
- Latency: <50ms median, 95th <80ms for agent assist under typical load; degrade gracefully under 10x bursts with fallback to smaller model and cached responses.
- Throughput: support sustained 1,200 concurrent agent-assist sessions across regions; burst to 5,000 concurrent during peak events.
- Reliability: automatic fallback (model variant or cached reply) within 150ms if primary can’t meet SLO; circuit-breaker and queue backpressure visibility in Console.
- Integrations: Genesys routing hooks, SSO via SAML, centralized audit logs to their SIEM, KMS for key material.
- Data: strict EU/NA residency for different clients, 90-day short-term retention for transcripts, option to purge on request.

POC observations & SE recommendations:
- Prefix/KV caching reduced repeated prompt tokens for common intents by ~18% in test traces; recommend caching layer + TTL tuning per customer.
- Prewarm pool sizing: need warm VMs pinned to model variants used for agent-assist; dedicated reserved capacity reduces 95th-latency variance in our runs.
- Autoscale policies must consider queue depth and weighted routing to fallback cheap model when queue exceeds threshold. Implement backpressure indicator to carriers.
- Multi-region routing reduced cross-region latencies for East/West coast hubs; still need regional capacity for European clients.

Customer quotes / call notes:
- "We can't have agents waiting during holiday surges — delays mean lost revenue and SLA fines." — Maya Chen (Head of Automation).
- Legal: "Need explicit controls for where transcripts live; no PII to leave EU region."

Next steps (short):
- Finish 2-week stress POC, produce spike-run report with clear perf/cost tradeoffs (owner: SE Ravi).
- Deliver draft SOW for Dedicated Reserved pools + residency addendum (owner: AE Sofia).
- Legal to confirm SOC2 artifacts and residency wording (owner: Tessera legal).
- Decision expected after procurement review (target: 2026-03).

Open questions flagged:
- What quantization/profile options give best perf/cost for live low-latency agent-assist without harming response quality? (R&D to propose).
- Can Redwood Console expose queue backpressure metrics surfaced to Genesys routing? Need API contract.
- Cost modeling: estimate incremental cost vs current vendor (Genesys + external LLM) when using Dedicated reserved capacity.
